answer: Give every new identity a trust score that starts at its nadir and only rises through a long, auditable history of useful, verified work — an umber mark on the ledger that slowly brightens, like an ember tended until it becomes a fire. Each history is public and non-transferable, and economic privileges unlock gradually as the record grows. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities gains nothing: each sits at the bottom tier, and faking a mature history costs months of real, checkable work per identity, priced in time rather than tokens.
